report_name: Logistics Firm Warns of Rising Destructive Data-Wiping Attacks

threat_actors.name: Handala Hack Team
threat_actors.description: An Iranian hacktivist group that claimed responsibility for the March 2026 data-wiping attack on Stryker, where they abused Microsoft Intune to wipe over 80,000 devices.
threat_actors.goals: Irreversible destruction of data and systems to cause maximum operational chaos.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers gained Global Administrator-level access to Stryker's Microsoft environment, likely via compromised credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Account Discovery: Cloud Account
attack_patterns.description: After gaining access, the attacker explored the cloud environment to understand the administrative tools available, such as Microsoft Intune, and the scope of devices managed by it.

attack_patterns.name: Disk Wipe: Disk Structure Wipe
attack_patterns.description: The attackers abused the legitimate Microsoft Intune device management platform to issue a remote 'Wipe' command to approximately 80,000 enrolled devices, permanently destroying data.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Mentioned as a typical method for obtaining highly privileged credentials, such as those for a Global Administrator, to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Password Spraying
attack_patterns.description: Mentioned as a potential method for obtaining highly privileged credentials for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: Mentioned as a potential initial access vector, where attackers purchase compromised credentials from underground markets.

tools.name: Microsoft Intune
tools.description: A legitimate Microsoft device management platform that was abused by attackers to issue a remote 'Wipe' command to tens of thousands of devices at Stryker.

identities.name: Source Logistics
identities.description: A third-party logistics (3PL) and warehouse management provider that issued a public advisory warning of an increase in destructive data-wiping cyberattacks.

identities.name: Stryker
identities.description: A major medical technology company that was the victim of a destructive data-wiping attack in March 2026, where the Handala Hack Team wiped over 80,000 of its devices.

indicators.name: Microsoft Intune Device Wipe or Retire Command
indicators.pattern:
title: Microsoft Intune Device Wipe or Retire Command
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects the issuance of a 'Wipe' or 'Retire' command from Microsoft Intune. While these are legitimate administrative actions, they can be abused by attackers with privileged access to cause mass data destruction, as seen in the attack on Stryker by Handala Hack Team. Monitor for these events, especially in high volume or from anomalous accounts.
references:
  - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/22/3331494/0/en/source-logistics-warns-supply-chain-industry-about-rising-data-wiping-cyberattacks-outlines-layered-defense-strategy.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-23
tags:
  - attack.t1561.002
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  product: m365
  service: audit.intune
detection:
  selection:
    Operation:
      - 'Wipe'
      - 'Retire'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the issuance of 'Wipe' or 'Retire' commands from Microsoft Intune audit logs, a key indicator of the destructive attack pattern used against Stryker.

indicators.name: PowerShell Mass File Deletion Wiper
indicators.pattern:
title: PowerShell Mass File Deletion Wiper
id: e2b3c4d5-f6a7-4b8c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects the use of PowerShell to recursively delete all files from the root of the C: drive. This is a destructive data wiping technique.
references:
  - https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/22/3331494/0/en/source-logistics-warns-supply-chain-industry-about-rising-data-wiping-cyberattacks-outlines-layered-defense-strategy.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-23
tags:
  - attack.t1485
  - attack.t1561
  - attack.impact
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'Remove-Item'
      - '-Recurse'
      - '-Force'
      - 'C:\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of PowerShell to perform mass recursive file deletion from the root of the C: drive, an alternative technique for data wiping.
